To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we introduce a novel method for discovering the underlying dynamics of a biological system from sparse experimental data and that we show the ability to identify the underlying mechanisms of the observed system.

BINNs are a new type of neural network that can approximate the solution of a PDE while simultaneously learning the form of the PDE and that BINNs can be used to guide the development of mechanistic mathematical models of cell biology assays.
BINNs can be used to learn mechanistic models from sparse experimental data and to guide the selection and parameter estimation of biologically relevant mechanistic models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of machine learning methods that can be applied in the context of in vitro cell biology assays.

the following questions: How can we leverage the power of neural networks to discover mechanistic forms of governing equations? Can we use neural networks to learn and discover the physical and biological mechanisms that govern the observed system?

the following questions: 1) Can we learn a PDE that describes a biological process from sparse experimental data and 2) Can we learn biologically meaningful mechanistic forms for the PDE that are interpretable and can guide the development of new hypothesis and future experiments?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BINNs provide a novel and promising framework to discover mechanistic models of biological systems from experimental data.
BINNs provide a novel approach for discovering the governing dynamics of biological systems that is both biologically informed and data driven.
BINNs can be used for mechanistic modeling from experimental data and provide a new way to discover underlying biological and physical mechanisms of a system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BINNs can be trained to approximate the dynamics of a system while simultaneously converging towards the solution of a governing PDE.
we are able to learn a model from sparse experimental data that can be used to predict the behavior of a system and that the learned model can be used to guide mechanistic modeling.
we have developed an end-to-end learning framework for mechanistic model discovery from sparse data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BINNs are capable of inferring biologically interpretable mechanisms from sparse experimental data and can serve as a tool to guide mechanistic modeling in cell biology.

by incorporating the governing PDE into the learning framework the resulting neural network can learn a biologically interpretable model from sparse data and can be used to guide the mechanistic model selection.

by using a biologically informed neural network to approximate experimental data, we can simultaneously discover a mechanistic model that can be used to predict the future dynamics of the biological process.
